meta.purpose: Career development and job preparation — role-by-role requirements, assessment practice and progression.

disclaimer.headline: Preparation, not a promise.
disclaimer.body: Nothing here guarantees employment, interview selection or a particular salary. A qualification such as CMA is a recognised credential, not a guaranteed job qualification, and hiring decisions depend on the employer's requirements, your experience, your performance in the process and market conditions. Treat every salary or package reference as an indicative, dated market observation to verify independently, not a commitment.

roles.name: Management Accountant
qualifications: CMA Intermediate or Final (in progress acceptable for entry roles)
Strong academic record in costing and financial accounting
technicalKnowledge: GST basics for input credit correctness
software: ERP: Tally Prime, SAP CO or Oracle
experienceExpectations: Prepared cost sheets or MIS for a real or simulated business
Can explain a variance to a plant manager
Has performed a physical stock verification or reconciliation
Understands month-end close sequencing
interviewQuestions: Walk me through how you would compute the cost of a product with three processes and normal loss in each.
A material price variance is favourable but the usage variance is adverse. What would you investigate first?
Why can absorption costing and marginal costing show different profit?
How would you decide whether to accept an export order at a price below domestic price?
What would you do if the plant head disputed your standard cost?
Explain how you would reconcile cost and financial accounts.
technicalAssessments: Prepare a cost sheet from a raw data set and identify the three largest cost drivers.
Compute material, labour and overhead variances from a standard cost card and actuals, and explain which to investigate.
caseStudies: A plant's cost per unit has risen 12% with stable input prices. Diagnose.
An order is offered at 8% below full cost with spare capacity available. Recommend with numbers.
resumeRequirements: One costing or MIS project with scope
portfolioProjects: Costing workbook with three products and variance analysis
Cost optimisation proposal with savings estimate
progression: Costing Executive → Management Accountant → Senior/Plant Finance Manager → Business Finance Head

roles.name: Financial Analyst
qualifications: CMA / CA / MBA Finance or equivalent
experienceExpectations: Built a model that someone else used
Written an analysis that led to a decision
Can defend every assumption in own work
interviewQuestions: Walk me through how a ₹1 increase in depreciation flows through the three statements.
Two companies have the same ROE. How would you decide which is the better business?
How would you analyse whether a company can service its debt?
What would make you distrust a company's reported profit?
Value a business with negative free cash flow.
Which is more important, margin or asset turnover? Defend your answer.
technicalAssessments: Build a three-statement model from provided historicals in 90 minutes.
Analyse three years of financials and present five insights with evidence.
caseStudies: A company's ROE is 18% but cash flow is negative. Explain how that is possible and whether it is sustainable.
Recommend whether to fund a ₹50 crore expansion using debt or equity.
resumeRequirements: Modelling and analysis projects with outputs
Any valuation work with methodology stated
portfolioProjects: Company research note with valuation range
progression: Financial Analyst → Senior Analyst → Finance Manager → FP&A Lead → Head of FP&A

roles.name: FP&A Analyst
qualifications: Evidence of budget or forecast ownership
experienceExpectations: Ran at least one budget or forecast cycle
Presented to a business head
Challenged a number and changed an outcome
interviewQuestions: How would you build a budget for a business you have never worked in?
The sales head says the forecast is wrong because the market is bad. How do you respond?
How do you forecast revenue for a business with no history?
What would you do if your forecast was consistently 8% too optimistic?
How would you explain a 3% cost overrun to a department that believes it is underfunded?
Which KPIs would you put on a one-page dashboard for a CFO?
technicalAssessments: Build a driver-based budget for a division from a business description in 90 minutes.
Given actuals and budget, produce a variance analysis with commentary and a 90-day action plan.
caseStudies: Revenue is 5% ahead of budget but EBITDA is 4% behind. Diagnose and recommend.
A department requests 20% more headcount. Evaluate the business case.
resumeRequirements: Budget/forecast scope in numbers (revenue, cost centres, headcount)
Outcome of an analysis you influenced
progression: FP&A Analyst → Senior FP&A → FP&A Manager → Head of FP&A → CFO track

roles.name: Cost Accountant
experienceExpectations: Prepared a cost statement per CAS format
Handled a stock count and valuation
Understood cost centre structures in an ERP
interviewQuestions: Which Cost Accounting Standards apply to a chemical manufacturer and why?
How would you cost a by-product?
Explain equivalent production with an example.
How do you avoid double counting overheads?
What is the difference between cost audit and financial audit?
How would you set up a cost centre structure from scratch?
technicalAssessments: Cost a multi-process product with normal and abnormal loss and present the cost per unit.
Prepare a cost statement in CAS format from a trial balance.
caseStudies: Overhead absorption rates have not been revised for two years. Assess the impact.
Two products share a process; recommend a joint cost allocation method and defend it.
portfolioProjects: Standard cost card and variance report
progression: Cost Accountant → Senior Cost Accountant → Costing Manager → Cost Audit Practice / Plant Finance Head

roles.name: Internal Auditor
experienceExpectations: Executed a control test end to end
Written a finding with root cause and recommendation
Handled a difficult auditee conversation
interviewQuestions: Walk me through how you would audit the procure-to-pay cycle.
What is the difference between a control deficiency and a material weakness?
How would you test whether all invoices are recorded?
The auditee says the finding is a one-off. How do you respond?
What analytics would you run across a full journal population?
How do you prioritise when you have 20 findings and half the budget?
technicalAssessments: Design a control test for revenue recognition and state the evidence required.
Given a journal extract, identify five suspicious patterns and explain why each matters.
caseStudies: Duplicate payments were found in one business unit. Recommend a control remediation plan.
The CFO asks you to soften a finding. What do you do?
progression: Internal Auditor → Senior Auditor → Audit Manager → Head of Internal Audit / Risk

roles.name: Financial Reporting Analyst
experienceExpectations: Prepared statements for a legal entity
Handled audit queries
Worked a close under a deadline
interviewQuestions: Explain how you would account for a lease under Ind AS 116.
How do you compute deferred tax on a revaluation?
Walk me through the consolidation of a subsidiary acquired mid-year.
Revenue is recognised over time — how do you audit the percentage complete?
What are the disclosure requirements for related party transactions?
How would you shorten a 12-day close to 6 days?
technicalAssessments: Prepare a consolidated balance sheet with one subsidiary and intra-group balances.
Given a fact pattern, state the Ind AS treatment and disclosure.
caseStudies: The auditor proposes a ₹2 crore provision. Assess whether to accept and how to communicate it.
A newly acquired entity uses a different revenue policy. Plan the alignment.
progression: Reporting Analyst → Senior → Reporting Manager → Controller → Group Controller

roles.name: Tax Analyst
experienceExpectations: Filed a return or reconciled a GST return
Handled a notice response
Maintained an amendment tracker
interviewQuestions: How would you determine whether a transaction is a supply of goods or services?
A vendor's GSTIN is invalid but the invoice is otherwise correct. Can you claim credit?
Explain the difference between exempt, nil-rated and zero-rated supplies.
How would you compute the arm's length price for a service transaction with a group company?
What is your process for tracking amendments?
A client wants to structure a transaction to avoid tax. How do you respond?
technicalAssessments: Compute GST liability and eligible ITC for a month from transaction data.
Compute total income and tax for an individual with five income sources.
caseStudies: A notice demands ₹80 lakh for an ITC mismatch. Build the response strategy.
Advise on GST implications of a works contract versus a composite supply.
portfolioProjects: Tax computation workbook with working notes
progression: Tax Analyst → Senior Tax Analyst → Tax Manager → Head of Tax / Indirect Tax Lead

roles.name: Business Analyst (Finance)
experienceExpectations: Influenced a decision with analysis
Mapped and improved a process
Worked with non-finance stakeholders
interviewQuestions: How would you evaluate whether a new product should be launched?
Sales wants a 10% discount to win a large customer. How do you assess it?
How do you gather requirements from a business head who does not know what they need?
Describe a process you improved and quantify the benefit.
How would you structure a business case for a new market entry?
What would you do if your analysis contradicted the CEO's view?
technicalAssessments: Build a business case for a proposed product launch with a break-even and a recommendation.
Map a broken process, identify three controls failures and recommend fixes.
caseStudies: A large customer demands a 12% price reduction or will leave. Evaluate.
Two departments claim the same cost savings. Resolve and report.
progression: Business Analyst → Senior Business Partner → Commercial Finance Manager → Business Finance Director

roles.name: Corporate Finance Analyst
qualifications: CMA / CA / MBA Finance / CFA (in progress)
experienceExpectations: Built a valuation model
Prepared an investment committee document
Participated in diligence
interviewQuestions: Walk me through a DCF and tell me which assumption matters most.
Why would two valuation methods give different answers?
How would you evaluate whether an acquisition creates value?
What is the difference between enterprise value and equity value?
How would you decide between debt and equity funding?
A target's working capital efficiency is worse than ours. What does that mean for price?
technicalAssessments: Value a target using DCF and comparables in 2 hours and present a recommendation.
Build an accretion/dilution analysis for a proposed acquisition.
caseStudies: Evaluate an acquisition at 9x EBITDA against a WACC of 12%.
Recommend a funding structure for a ₹200 crore capex programme.
progression: Analyst → Associate → Manager → VP / Head of Corporate Development

roles.name: Finance Transformation Analyst
qualifications: CMA / CA / MBA with process or systems exposure
Evidence of process redesign or automation
experienceExpectations: Documented a process end to end
Delivered an automation or improvement
Managed stakeholder change
interviewQuestions: How would you decide which finance processes to automate first?
What controls must exist in an automated reconciliation?
A process is broken — how do you know whether to fix, automate or eliminate it?
How do you measure the benefit of an automation programme?
What are the risks of removing a manual review step?
How would you manage resistance from a team whose work is being automated?
technicalAssessments: Produce an automation business case with quantified benefit and risk for one process.
Design the target-state process and control matrix for a close process.
caseStudies: Close takes 12 days; target is 5. Build the roadmap.
An RPA bot failed silently for a week. Design the controls to prevent recurrence.
progression: Analyst → Process Lead → Transformation Manager → Head of Finance Systems / GPO

roles.name: Financial Data Analyst
qualifications: CMA / CA / B.Tech / B.Sc with analytics evidence
experienceExpectations: Built a dashboard used by others
Written SQL against a real schema
Cleaned a messy dataset and documented the process
interviewQuestions: How would you find duplicate invoices across a million rows?
Explain the difference between a star schema and a flat table, and when to use each.
A dashboard shows revenue up 10% but finance reports 4%. How do you investigate?
How would you detect an anomaly in monthly cost data?
What would you do about missing values in a key financial field?
How do you prevent a dashboard from misleading its users?
technicalAssessments: Write five SQL queries against a finance schema, including a window function.
Build a dashboard from a provided dataset and defend every measure definition.
caseStudies: Two source systems report different revenue. Reconcile and recommend a single definition and governance.
A forecast model has drifted for three months. Diagnose and fix.
progression: Data Analyst → Senior Analyst → Analytics Manager → Head of Finance Analytics

companyPreparation.name: Big Four professional services
whatTheyLookFor: Ability to work in a team on tight deadlines
preparation: Practise case interviews with a timer
Prepare two technical stories per competency
Know the firm's service lines and recent publications
Be able to explain one standard in depth
watchOuts: Long working hours during season — be honest about capacity

companyPreparation.name: Consulting firms
preparation: Practise 30 cases, focusing on profitability, market entry and cost reduction
Read industry reports on the target sector
watchOuts: Case interviews reward structure over the right answer

companyPreparation.name: Banks and financial institutions
process: Technical interview on credit and financial analysis
preparation: Understand ratio covenants and their purpose
Be ready to assess a company's repayment capacity in ten minutes
watchOuts: Compliance culture is strict — never imply flexibility on regulatory matters
Sales-linked roles may be presented as analytical roles

companyPreparation.name: Corporate finance departments
preparation: Know the company's business model and recent results
Be ready to discuss a variance you explained
watchOuts: Roles can be narrow — ask about scope in the interview
Month-end and year-end intensity is normal

portfolioGuidance.principle: Three excellent artefacts beat ten unfinished ones. Every artefact must state the business problem, the data, the method, the result, the limitations and the recommendation.
portfolioGuidance.presentation: Host on GitHub with a README per project. Use synthetic data only. Include a limitations section and a 'what I would do differently' reflection — it signals judgement.
